domestic.remittances: Re-checked this cycle, unchanged: FY26 remittances hit an all-time record $41.6bn, +8.6% YoY vs $38.3bn in FY25 (Saudi Arabia $9.78bn, UAE $8.81bn, UK $6.33bn, EU $5.23bn top sources); SBP projects $44bn in FY27 (https://www.thenews.pk/story/1424957-fy26-remittances-hit-416bn-showing-86-yearly-growth, https://www.geo.tv/latest/672203-workers-remittances-rise-86-to-416bn-in-fy26). GCC supplies well over half of inflows -- the live Hormuz blockade/naval-toll standoff is a forward risk to this channel via Gulf labour-market and freight disruption, not yet visible in the printed data.
domestic.current_account: Re-checked this cycle: no official full-FY26 (Jul-Jun) current account print from SBP yet. Latest hard cumulative figure remains the 11-month Jul-May FY26 surplus of ~$255mn (vs a $1.62bn deficit in the same period a year earlier); May 2026 alone posted a $459mn monthly surplus. SBP Governor Jameel Ahmad has guided the full FY26 current account to close 'slightly in surplus' for a second consecutive year (https://www.brecorder.com/news/40429111, https://www.dawn.com/news/2008684). This guidance predates the live Hormuz conflict: since >80% of Pakistan's crude imports transit the strait, Trump's 20% Hormuz cargo toll and renewed naval blockade -- in effect since 2026-07-14 4pm ET -- is a forward-looking FY27-Q1 import-bill risk not captured in any FY26 print (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/14/oil-prices-today-brent-wti-hormuz-trump-toll-iran.html).

global_read: Global tape per global.json (17:32 snapshot): Brent $86.57 (+3.93% 1d, +4.09% 1mo) and WTI $80.02 (+2.41% 1d) both at fresh multi-week highs as the Hormuz blockade/toll moved from announced to in-effect; VIX 17.51 (+2.04% 1d) only mildly elevated, not a broad panic reading; gold +0.87% (safe-haven bid persists, though -6.84% 1mo); S&P -0.79%/Dow -0.26% (developed-market equities not panicking); PKR/USD 277.73 (+0.31% 1d) still orderly; DXY 101.02 (-0.26% 1d) soft. Same signature as prior cycles today: the shock is landing disproportionately on Pakistan via the oil-import/current-account channel -- and directly on PSX, which per today's confirmed session close fell far more than any global benchmark -- rather than through a broad, diversified global risk-off.

Selling was broad-based across banks, cement, fertilizer, E&P and OMCs, continuing the pattern from 2026-07-13's -1.27% close (https://www.brecorder.com/news/40429928/selling-grips-psx-kse-100-tumbles-nearly-5000-points-as-us-reimposes-naval-blockade-on-iran, https://tribune.com.pk/story/2618166/hormuz-tensions-send-psx-tumbling-over-4200-points)

Hormuz conflict re-verified as still live and escalating this cycle with fresh sources: Trump's 20% Hormuz cargo toll and renewed naval blockade of Iranian shipping took effect 2026-07-14 at 4pm ET ('reimbursement...for the job of providing safety and security'); a 20% toll is estimated at ~$32mn per tanker, adding ~$16/barrel per FT figures cited by CNBC; crossings through the strait have reportedly dropped more than half from the prior week; the mid-June ceasefire is effectively over after repeated strikes -- a live, contested chokepoint standoff, not resolved (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/14/oil-prices-today-brent-wti-hormuz-trump-toll-iran.html, https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/13/trump-iran-hormuz-strait-charge-reimburse.html)

REGIME CALL: risk-off, held and reinforced. Rationale -- (1) the Hormuz conflict remains live, contested and now physically in effect (blockade/toll enforcement began today, strait crossings reportedly down more than half week-on-week); (2) Brent/WTI both at fresh multi-week highs; (3) PSX's own tape closed today down 3.56%, its second straight sharply negative session, deeper than the global risk tape (VIX only +2.04% 1d, S&P -0.79%) -- confirming the shock is landing on Pakistan disproportionately via the oil-import/current-account channel; (4) desk georisk radar holds at 59/100 moderate with conflict stress maxed; (5) domestic anchors (SBP hold, easing CPI, on-track IMF program, adequate/growing reserves, record remittances, an FY26 current account guided to a marginal surplus, sub-policy-rate T-bill yields) remain genuinely constructive and argue against a capitulation-level panic read, but none of this offsets a live, unresolved chokepoint conflict hitting Pakistan's oil-import bill directly. Net: stay risk-off, defensive/beneficiary sectors only, max 2 new setups per desk rules, tight monitoring of existing positions.

favored: E&P (upstream oil & gas -- direct beneficiary of higher realized crude/gas prices, though MARI/OGDC/PPL have still traded red alongside the broad market on index-wide selling; a realized-price economics case, not immunity from the selloff)
banks (quality/defensive, high-rate carry, though also named among the day's biggest index drags on broad-based selling -- watch for stabilization before treating as a safe harbor)
fertilizer (domestic-demand defensive, low direct oil-import beta)
avoid: OMCs (inventory/margin and circular-debt risk from volatile, weekly-repriced fuel costs amid a live oil spike)
autos (imported-input cost + weaker consumer demand under fuel/inflation pressure)
cement (energy-intensive, imported coal/fuel cost exposure, named among today's laggards)
textiles/exporters (Gulf freight-cost and input-cost exposure amid an active Hormuz blockade)
refineries (crude-cost volatility and margin risk despite the announced $6bn refinery-upgrade fast-track plan, a multi-year structural story, not a near-term offset)
power (fuel-cost pass-through and circular-debt sensitivity amid the oil spike)
